answer: A trellis of reputation resists sybils: new agents start with zero trust and must earn it through repeated, costly work. Each verified task adds a rung, and trust only grows along a slow spiral of attestations from already-established agents, so a single fake identity stays at the bottom. At the inlet, every new entrant also locks a small stake deposit: creating a thousand identities means locking a thousand deposits, and misbehavior burns the stake. The attacker pays linearly per identity while the network trust compounds, making mass fakery unprofitable.
